reader.where: What you need, terminal Scene caption "Make an empty practice folder and turn it into a repo, one command per line." (line 48), with Try step 2 (lines 190-197) and the Cheat sheet row "`cd` into your repo, then `claude`" (line 255)
reader.problem: Two problems in one place. First, nothing ever says what `mkdir` and `cd` do. A Visitor who barely uses a terminal meets them in the Scene, in Try step 2 and in the Cheat sheet's "`cd` into your repo", which only works if you know `cd`. This is the one Lesson where a beginner could learn them, since other Lessons' Trys use them without a gloss. Second, the Scene shows the same `mkdir agent-practice`, `cd`, `git init`, `claude` steps that Try step 2 runs again. A reader who types along with the Scene gets an error at Try step 2: "mkdir: agent-practice: File exists" on a Mac, or New-Item's "An item with the specified name ... already exists" in PowerShell. A newcomer will read that as a failure.
reader.evidence: Lines 49-54 (Scene) and 193-196 (Try step 2) are the same four commands. Line 255: "| Start a session | `cd` into your repo, then `claude` |". No line glosses mkdir or cd. Other Lessons use them unexplained: 03-skills.md:265-266 (`mkdir skills-practice`, `cd skills-practice`), 05-domain-modeling.md:248-249, 06-prototype.md:229-230. Scene captions don't add to the 1,400-word prose count (lint-lesson.mjs:65).
reader.fix: Line 48: "# Make an empty practice folder and turn it into a repo, one command per line: mkdir makes the folder, cd moves you into it, and git init starts tracking it. You'll run these in the Try below, so there's no need to type them now."
